AnalyticsOverview.description:
/admin/analytics/overview response — one payload for the whole page.

`daily_totals` and `by_topic` cover the last `days` UTC days; `trending` is the top 20 by
views in that window, each with a per-day `sparkline` over the same window; `all_time_top`
is from article_metrics.view_count and has no window.

post.description:
Unauthenticated — collapses the SSR-initialization chain (frontend/lib/server/
ssr-fetch.ts: guest token, then GET /topics + GET /languages, 2 serial round trips
for a first-time visitor) into one. Always mints a fresh guest access token
(stateless JWT sign, no DB hit) rather than accepting/validating an existing one —
a simple, argument-free contract is worth the occasional unused token when the
caller already held a session or guest credential of its own.

Proxies to the chatbot-plugin service's own OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions`.

chatbot-plugin's own Swagger UI is unavailable — `CHAT_SERVICE_URL` is not configured.

get.description:
CPU flamebearer for one app (`service`) over [start, end] (unix seconds) — the root
span's own time window (RunWaterfallDialog), not a per-sub-span query: profiling is CPU
sampling, and a whole-request window has enough samples to be statistically meaningful in
a way a handful-of-milliseconds child span wouldn't.

parameters.description: Which app's profile to query — "backend" (default, backward compatible with callers that never passed this) or "scraper". Both push to the same Grafana Cloud Profiles instance, distinguished by their own pyroscope.configure(application_name=...).
parameters.name: service

schema.description: Which app's profile to query — "backend" (default, backward compatible with callers that never passed this) or "scraper". Both push to the same Grafana Cloud Profiles instance, distinguished by their own pyroscope.configure(application_name=...).
schema.title: Service

parameters.description: Narrows the flamebearer to CPU samples tagged with this OTel span_id by to_thread_profiled() (backend) / run_tagged_for_profiling() (scraper) — currently only search_service.py's sync-Session DB calls (backend) and ScrapeExecutor's fetch/discover tasks (scraper) tag their samples this way, so any other span_id returns an empty (but successful) flamebearer, same as a time window with no samples. `start`/`end` still bound the query the same as without this filter (see the padding-window comment below) — this narrows *which* samples in that window count, not the window itself.
parameters.name: span_id

Approve many suggestions in one request instead of the frontend firing
one sequential POST per suggestion (which also used to abort entirely on
the first cascade-induced 404 — see _approve_suggestion_row). Mirrors

failure doesn't block the rest.
